rules.title: Automatic forwarding to external domains is disabled
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: Every remote domain (including the default `*` entry) must have automatic forwarding disabled so mailbox rules and forwarding cannot silently send mail to external recipients. Auto-forwarding is a common data-exfiltration technique after account compromise.
rules.remediation: Exchange admin center > Mail flow > Remote domains > open each domain (including Default) > uncheck 'Allow automatic forwarding'. Or: `Set-RemoteDomain -Identity Default -AutoForwardEnabled $false`.
rules.impact: Users can no longer auto-forward mail to external addresses.

rules.title: SPF record authorizes Exchange Online for each custom domain
rules.name: domain
rules.description: Each verified custom domain must publish an SPF record that includes spf.protection.outlook.com (or outlook.com), designating Exchange Online as an approved sender. Domains using a redirect modifier are treated as delegated and accepted. Initial onmicrosoft.com domains are excluded.
rules.remediation: Publish a TXT record for each domain such as `v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all`, adding any other legitimate senders.

rules.title: DKIM signing is enabled for all custom domains
rules.name: Domain
rules.description: DKIM signing must be enabled for each custom domain so recipients can verify message integrity and sender domain. Initial onmicrosoft.com domains are signed automatically by Microsoft and are excluded. Parked (non-sending) domains cannot be excluded by this check.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Email authentication settings > DKIM > select the domain > enable signing. Or `Set-DkimSigningConfig -Identity <domain> -Enabled $true`.

rules.title: DKIM selector CNAME records are published in DNS
rules.name: domain
rules.description: Both Microsoft DKIM selector CNAME records (selector1 and selector2) must exist for each custom domain so signing and key rotation work. The source test validates the active selector only; this check requires both.
rules.remediation: In your DNS zone create CNAME records `selector1._domainkey.<domain>` and `selector2._domainkey.<domain>` pointing to the values shown in the Defender portal DKIM page.

rules.title: A DMARC record is published for each custom domain
rules.name: domain
rules.description: A DMARC policy must be published for every second-level domain so receivers know how to handle unauthenticated mail that spoofs your domain.
rules.remediation: Publish a TXT record at `_dmarc.<domain>`, for example `v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@<domain>`.

rules.title: DMARC policy is set to reject
rules.name: domain
rules.description: The DMARC policy (p=) must be `reject` so spoofed messages are blocked rather than delivered or only quarantined.
rules.remediation: Move the `p=` tag of the `_dmarc` TXT record to `reject` after monitoring reports and fixing legitimate senders.

rules.title: DMARC aggregate reports are sent to CISA
rules.name: domain
rules.description: US federal agency control: the DMARC rua tag must include reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov. Not relevant to non-government tenants.
rules.remediation: Add `mailto:reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov` to the `rua=` list of the `_dmarc` TXT record.

rules.title: SMTP AUTH is disabled organization-wide
rules.description: Authenticated SMTP client submission (SMTP AUTH) uses legacy basic authentication that is easy to abuse with password spraying. It should be disabled tenant-wide and enabled only per mailbox where unavoidable.
rules.remediation: Exchange admin center > Settings > Mail flow > turn off SMTP AUTH, or `Set-TransportConfig -SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled $true`.
rules.impact: Devices and apps that send mail with SMTP AUTH stop working unless re-enabled per mailbox.

rules.title: Contact folders are not shared with all domains
rules.name: Name
rules.description: No enabled sharing policy may share contact folders with all domains (`*`) or anonymously. Evaluation note: the list-valued Domains property must match when any entry matches.
rules.remediation: Exchange admin center > Settings > Sharing > Individual sharing policies > edit each policy and remove contact sharing for `*` / Anonymous (or disable the policy).

rules.title: Calendar details are not shared with all domains
rules.name: Name
rules.description: No enabled sharing policy may share calendar details with all domains (`*`) or anonymously. Evaluation note: the list-valued Domains property must match when any entry matches.
rules.remediation: Exchange admin center > Settings > Sharing > Individual sharing policies > edit each policy and remove calendar sharing for `*` / Anonymous (or disable the policy).

rules.title: The Standard preset security policy exists for anti-spam policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: CISA expects the Standard preset security policy to be configured so anti-spam policies follow Microsoft recommended settings. Passes when a policy of recommended type Standard exists.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset Security Policies > turn on Standard and Strict protection and scope them to users.

rules.title: The Strict preset security policy exists for anti-spam policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: CISA expects the Strict preset security policy to be configured so anti-spam policies follow Microsoft recommended settings. Passes when a policy of recommended type Strict exists.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset Security Policies > turn on Standard and Strict protection and scope them to users.

rules.title: The Standard preset security policy exists for anti-phishing policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: CISA expects the Standard preset security policy to be configured so anti-phishing policies follow Microsoft recommended settings. Passes when a policy of recommended type Standard exists.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset Security Policies > turn on Standard and Strict protection and scope them to users.

rules.title: The Strict preset security policy exists for anti-phishing policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: CISA expects the Strict preset security policy to be configured so anti-phishing policies follow Microsoft recommended settings. Passes when a policy of recommended type Strict exists.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset Security Policies > turn on Standard and Strict protection and scope them to users.

rules.title: The Standard preset security policy exists for Safe Links policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: CISA expects the Standard preset security policy to be configured so Safe Links policies follow Microsoft recommended settings. Passes when a policy of recommended type Standard exists.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset Security Policies > turn on Standard and Strict protection and scope them to users.

rules.title: The Strict preset security policy exists for Safe Links policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: CISA expects the Strict preset security policy to be configured so Safe Links policies follow Microsoft recommended settings. Passes when a policy of recommended type Strict exists.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset Security Policies > turn on Standard and Strict protection and scope them to users.

rules.title: The Standard preset security policy exists for anti-malware policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: CISA expects the Standard preset security policy to be configured so anti-malware policies follow Microsoft recommended settings. Passes when a policy of recommended type Standard exists.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset Security Policies > turn on Standard and Strict protection and scope them to users.

rules.title: The Strict preset security policy exists for anti-malware policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: CISA expects the Strict preset security policy to be configured so anti-malware policies follow Microsoft recommended settings. Passes when a policy of recommended type Strict exists.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset Security Policies > turn on Standard and Strict protection and scope them to users.

rules.title: An anti-malware policy has the common attachment filter enabled
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one anti-malware policy must enable the common attachments filter (EnableFileFilter), which blocks risky file types by true file type as well as extension.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Anti-malware > edit the policy > enable 'Enable the common attachments filter'.

rules.title: An anti-malware policy enforces the disallowed file type filter
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: Disallowed file types must be determined and enforced; at least one anti-malware policy must have the common attachments filter turned on.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Anti-malware > edit the policy > enable the common attachments filter and review the selected file types.

rules.title: Click-to-run file types (.exe, .cmd, .vbe) are blocked
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one anti-malware policy must enable the common attachments filter and include the cmd, exe and vbe file types.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-malware policy > Common attachments filter > select file types cmd, exe and vbe (the Standard/Strict preset policies already include them).

rules.title: A policy has full impersonation protection enabled
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one enabled anti-phishing policy must have automatic impersonation protection with organization domain, targeted domain and targeted user protection on.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Anti-phishing > edit the policy > Phishing threshold & protection > turn on user and domain impersonation and organization domain protection, and add protected users/domains.

rules.title: A policy displays impersonation safety tips
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one enabled anti-phishing policy must show safety tips for similar domains, similar users and unusual characters.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-phishing policy > Actions > Safety tips & indicators > enable all three tips.

rules.title: A policy has mailbox intelligence protection enabled
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one enabled anti-phishing policy must use mailbox intelligence and mailbox intelligence protection.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-phishing policy > Phishing threshold & protection > enable mailbox intelligence and 'Enable intelligence for impersonation protection'.

rules.title: No connection filter IP allow list exists
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: Connection filter IP allow lists bypass spam filtering and should not be used.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Anti-spam > Connection filter policy > clear the IP Allow list.

rules.title: Connection filter safe list is disabled
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: The connection filter 'safe list' option bypasses filtering for senders Microsoft deems safe and should be off.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-spam > Connection filter policy > Edit > uncheck 'Turn on safe list'.

rules.title: Mailbox auditing is enabled
rules.description: Mailbox auditing must not be disabled organization-wide so mailbox activity is recorded for investigations.
rules.remediation: `Set-OrganizationConfig -AuditDisabled $false`.

rules.title: Purview Audit (Standard) logging is enabled
rules.description: The unified audit log must be turned on so user and admin activity across Microsoft 365 is recorded.
rules.remediation: Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity, or `Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true`.

rules.title: Preset spam policies move spam and high confidence spam to Junk or Quarantine
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: No Standard or Strict preset anti-spam policy found
rules.description: The Standard and Strict preset anti-spam policies must move spam and high-confidence spam to the Junk Email folder or quarantine. Existence of both presets is checked by the 14.1 rules.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-spam policies > edit policy > Actions > set spam and high-confidence spam to 'Move to Junk Email folder' or 'Quarantine message'.

rules.title: No allowed sender domains in anti-spam policies
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: Allowed sender domains bypass spam filtering and can be abused by spoofing; none should be configured in inbound anti-spam policies.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-spam policies > edit policy > Allowed and blocked senders and domains > remove all allowed domains.

rules.title: A Safe Links policy scans URLs in email
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one Safe Links policy must have Safe Links protection for email messages enabled.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Safe Links > edit policy > turn on Safe Links for email.

rules.title: A Safe Links policy scans direct download links
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one Safe Links policy must have real-time URL scanning (ScanUrls) enabled so direct download links are checked.
rules.remediation: Safe Links policy > 'Scan URLs' / real-time URL scanning > enable.

rules.title: A Safe Links policy tracks user clicks
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one Safe Links policy must record user clicks on URLs.
rules.remediation: Safe Links policy > 'Track user clicks' > enable.

rules.title: 'External sharing' of calendars is not available
rules.name: Name
rules.description: No enabled sharing policy may allow calendar details to be shared with all domains or anonymously. Evaluation note: the list-valued Domains property must match when any entry matches.
rules.remediation: Exchange admin center > Settings > Sharing > edit individual sharing policies to remove calendar sharing with `*` / Anonymous, or `Set-SharingPolicy -Identity <name> -Enabled $false`.

rules.title: Customer Lockbox is enabled
rules.description: Customer Lockbox requires your approval before Microsoft support engineers can access tenant content.
rules.remediation: Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Security & privacy > Customer lockbox > require approval, or `Set-OrganizationConfig -CustomerLockBoxEnabled $true`.

rules.title: Common attachment types filter is enabled (default policy)
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: The default anti-malware policy must enable the common attachments filter and block all CIS-listed default file extensions.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-malware > Default policy > enable the common attachments filter and select all recommended file types.

rules.title: Notifications for internal users sending malware are enabled (default policy)
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: The default anti-malware policy must notify an administrator when an internal sender is detected sending malware, with a notification address set.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-malware > Default policy > Notifications > enable admin notification for internal senders and enter the admin address.

rules.title: Safe Attachments built-in protection policy blocks and quarantines to admin only
rules.name: Name
rules.description: The Built-In Protection Policy for Safe Attachments must be enabled with action Block and the AdminOnlyAccessPolicy quarantine policy.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Threat policies > Safe Attachments > Built-in protection > set response to Block and quarantine policy to AdminOnlyAccessPolicy.

rules.title: Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams is enabled
rules.description: Safe Attachments must be on for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams, with Safe Documents enabled and click-through on Protected View blocked.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Threat policies > Safe Attachments > Global settings > enable ATP for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams and Safe Documents; disable 'Allow people to click through Protected View'.

rules.title: Outbound spam policy notifies administrators (default policy)
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: Default outbound spam policy not found
rules.description: The default outbound spam policy must BCC suspicious outbound mail and notify admins about outbound spam.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-spam > Anti-spam outbound policy (Default) > enable 'Send a copy of suspicious outbound messages' and 'Notify specific people'.

rules.title: Default anti-phishing policy is configured as recommended
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: The default anti-phishing policy must be enabled with mailbox intelligence, intelligence protection, spoof intelligence, and a phishing threshold of 2 or higher.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Threat policies > Anti-phishing > Default policy > enable mailbox intelligence and spoof intelligence and set the phishing email threshold to 2 (Aggressive) or higher.

rules.title: DKIM is enabled for all Exchange Online domains
rules.name: Domain
rules.description: DKIM signing must be enabled for every custom domain. Initial onmicrosoft.com domains are excluded; parked domains cannot be excluded by this check.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Email authentication settings > DKIM > enable signing for each domain.

rules.title: DKIM selector CNAME records are published for all custom domains
rules.name: domain
rules.description: Both DKIM selector CNAME records must be present in DNS for each custom domain. The source test validates the active selector only; this check requires both.
rules.remediation: Create `selector1._domainkey.<domain>` and `selector2._domainkey.<domain>` CNAME records with the values from the Defender portal.

rules.title: Comprehensive attachment filtering is applied
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: At least one anti-malware policy with the common attachments filter enabled must block every CIS Level 2 file extension. The source test unions the extensions across all file-filter-enabled policies; this check requires them all in a single policy.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-malware > edit the policy > common attachments filter > select all CIS-recommended file types.

rules.title: Connection filter IP allow list is not used (default policy)
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: Default connection filter policy not found
rules.description: The default connection filter policy must have an empty IP Allow list.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-spam > Connection filter policy (Default) > remove all IP Allow list entries.

rules.title: Connection filter safe list is off (default policy)
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: Default connection filter policy not found
rules.description: The default connection filter policy must not use the Microsoft safe list.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Anti-spam > Connection filter policy (Default) > uncheck 'Turn on safe list'.

rules.title: Zero-hour auto purge for Microsoft Teams is on
rules.name: Identity
rules.description: ZAP for Teams removes messages later found to be malicious or phishing.
rules.remediation: Defender portal > Settings > Email & collaboration > Microsoft Teams protection > turn on zero-hour auto purge, or `Set-TeamsProtectionPolicy -ZapEnabled $true`.

rules.title: Microsoft 365 audit log search is enabled
rules.description: Audit log search must be enabled so activity is recorded and searchable.
rules.remediation: Purview portal > Audit > Start recording, or `Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true`.

rules.title: Additional storage providers are restricted in Outlook on the web
rules.name: Identity
rules.empty_message: Default OWA mailbox policy not found
rules.description: The default OWA mailbox policy must not allow additional storage providers such as Dropbox or Box.
rules.remediation: `Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -Identity OwaMailboxPolicy-Default -AdditionalStorageProvidersAvailable $false`.

rules.title: MailTips for external recipients are enabled
rules.description: MailTips warn users when they address external recipients, reducing accidental data disclosure.
rules.remediation: `Set-OrganizationConfig -MailTipsExternalRecipientsTipsEnabled $true`.

rules.title: Users cannot install Outlook add-ins
rules.name: Name
rules.description: The Default Role Assignment Policy must not include the roles My Custom Apps, My Marketplace Apps or My ReadWriteMailbox Apps, which let users install add-ins that can read mailbox content.
rules.remediation: Exchange admin center > Roles > User roles > Default Role Assignment Policy > uncheck the three app roles.
rules.impact: Users can no longer self-install Outlook add-ins.

rules.title: No transport rule sets SCL to -1
rules.name: Name
rules.description: Transport rules that set SCL to -1 bypass spam and phish filtering for matching mail and can be abused.
rules.remediation: Exchange admin center > Mail flow > Rules > remove or change rules that set the spam confidence level to -1 (bypass spam filtering).

rules.title: Modern authentication is enabled for Exchange Online
rules.description: Modern authentication (OAuth2) must be enabled so clients can use MFA and Conditional Access.
rules.remediation: `Set-OrganizationConfig -OAuth2ClientProfileEnabled $true`.

rules.title: Direct Send is rejected
rules.description: Direct Send lets unauthenticated devices send mail as your domain to your tenant; it should be rejected unless required.
rules.remediation: `Set-OrganizationConfig -RejectDirectSend $true`.
rules.impact: Devices that relay unauthenticated via your MX endpoint stop working; move them to authenticated submission or a connector.
